memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But commission Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, for he will lead this people across and will cause them to inherit the land that you will see. So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor. - Deut 3:28-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's instruction to Moses in the face of his disappointment is remarkable: "Commission Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him." Rather than dwelling on his own unfulfilled desire, Moses was to invest in the leader who would carry on after him. He would not enter the land, but he could prepare the one who would lead the people in. His legacy would continue through Joshua.

This is a beautiful picture of finishing well. Moses could have spent his final days in bitter regret, focused on what he would miss. Instead, God called him to a selfless task: to strengthen his successor for the work ahead. Moses' role was not over; it had simply shifted from leading to equipping the next generation. There is great dignity in preparing others to succeed where we ourselves will not go.

This challenges us to think beyond ourselves. The work of God is bigger than any one of us and continues from generation to generation. Part of finishing well is investing in those who come after us — encouraging, strengthening, and equipping them to carry the work forward. We are links in a chain, receiving from those before and passing on to those after. Paul urged Timothy to entrust the gospel to faithful people who would teach others also (2 Tim 2:2).

Even in disappointment, Moses lifted his eyes to the good of others and the ongoing purposes of God. That is a life well lived. And behind it all is the assurance that God's plan does not depend on any one servant; it marches on faithfully toward its fulfilment in Christ. Whatever season you are in, consider how you might encourage and strengthen those coming after you, playing your part in the story God is writing across the generations.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How can you invest in and encourage those who will come after you?
2. Does Moses' example challenge you to think beyond your own role?
3. How does knowing God's work continues across generations bring you peace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to finish well by investing in others, encouraging and strengthening those who come after me. Thank You that Your work does not depend on me alone but marches on faithfully toward its fulfilment in Christ. Amen.
